Born in 1981 in Berlin, Germany. After finishing school, she spent two years travelling the world before studying audiovisual communication in Amsterdam and animation at the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts. Her graduation film, Der kleine Vogel und das Blatt , premiered in the 2012 Berlinale Generation section, as did her three following films about the little bird and, most recently, Tümpel (co-directed with Eva Rust). Her imaginative, poetic films for children also delight adults and have won over 30 international awards including the Goldener Spatz from the eponymous children’s media festival in Germany.

Amay Mehrishi is an Indian filmmaker based in London and a recent graduate of the MA Filmmaking programme at the London Film School. He previously earned a bachelor’s degree in marketing and innovation from the National University of Singapore, which shaped his understanding of audience and narrative – skills that now enrich his filmmaking practice. Drawn to stories that capture human flaws and nuanced emotions with a commitment to realism, Amay works fluidly across fiction and documentary as both a director and producer. Currently developing his next documentary project, he seeks to engage more deeply with his roots, exploring stories with relentless curiosity.

The director completed an MFA in film directing and screenwriting at Columbia University in 2024. Her work primarily focuses on comedies and explores stories of individuals striving to fit into a bewildering, often incomprehensible world. Her short film Say Something , which screened at multiple international festivals, follows a teenage girl who fakes speaking in tongues to impress her crush at church. Speedy! won an Indian Paintbrush Productions grant.

Born in Guadalajara, Mexico in 1999, he studied audiovisual arts at the University of Guadalajara. His work approaches cinema from a queer perspective and within the context of independent filmmaking, with a particular interest in intimate and everyday processes. Cuando llegue a casa is his graduation film and his first short as a director.

Born in Caserta, Italy in 2000. He is the founder of Onirica Pictures, an independent production collective with which he has directed, produced and written several short films which have screened across Italy. After graduating with a degree in screenwriting from the Civica Scuola di Cinema Luchino Visconti in Milan, he is currently studying anthropology at Sapienza University in Rome.

Born in Guangdong, China, Beidi studied journalism at the University of Oregon, and film and television production at the University of Southern California. Her graduation film Wax and Wane won Best Global Short at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival and Best Female Director at the Indie Short Fest. Her works address the intersection of the body, memory and social systems.

The director has primarily worked in advertising and has already received several significant industry awards, including the Grand Prix at the Cíclope Latino and the award for best Peruvian director at El Ojo de Iberoamerica. Allá en el cielo is his first short film. He is currently developing his first feature film, El vuelo de las hojas .

The London based director is celebrated as one of the biggest filmmaking talents to emerge from the Netherlands in recent years. Born in Tokyo in 1989, he studied at the European Film College in Denmark and graduated from the Netherlands Film Academy in 2013. Mees was twice nominated for a Crystal Bear at the Berlinale for his short films A Hole in my Heart and Even Cowboys Get to Cry . Mees won two Golden Calves (Netherlands Film Festival) for his film We Will Never Be Royals . He was selected for the Cinéfondation Résidence by the Cannes Film Festival, where he wrote his first feature film, Paradise Drifters , which premiered at the Berlinale in 2020.

Born in South Korea in 1985, she graduated from the Department of Printmaking at Hongik University, worked as an artist in Seoul and participated in several film workshops. Ghwa The Last Name won the Chung Jung-won award for Best Short Film at the Blue Dragon Film Awards. En Route To is her graduation project from the pre-production and feature film production programme run by the Korean Academy of Film Arts.

Born in 1986 in Munich, Germany, the writer and director studied philosophy at the Sorbonne in Paris but is an autodidact as a filmmaker. His mid-length film Jesus Egon Christus , which he co-directed with David Vajda, premiered in the Perspektive Deutsches Kino section of the Berlinale in 2021 and went on to screen at festivals including the International Film Festival Rotterdam.

Premiering at Sundance earlier this year, Paloma Schneideman’s coming-of-age debut launches our festival with a tender portrait of 14-year-old Sid, as she tentatively traverses insecurity, identity and desire during the summer of 2006.
An intimate and warm story of a life entwined with a deep-rooted sense of belonging, and the inconvenience of aging in a world that continues to move at pace.

When Kabul's only female camerawoman is given a career opportunity by the last man she expected, she finds herself falling for someone in a city that is about to fall itself. A funny, warm and deeply political romance from one of the most exciting voices in world cinema.
A hand-drawn wonder brimming with imagination and warmth, Arco is the kind of film that reminds you of the joy of discovery.
